title: riot
one_liner: A lightweight Python socket server and curses-based client for tracking taxi driver performance ratings.
what_it_is: riot is a distributed system for collecting real-time feedback on taxi drivers. It consists of a central server that stores ride data in SQLite, interactive terminal clients for drivers to log rides and toggle 'thumbs up' ratings (promptness, cleanliness, friendliness), and a reporting agent that generates top-10 lists over rolling 48-hour windows.
how_its_built: The system is built with Python 2 standard libraries. The server uses raw TCP sockets to accept JSON payloads and writes directly to a local SQLite database. The client uses the `curses` library for a text-based user interface (TUI) to manage ride states and rating toggles before sending JSON data over TCP. Reporting is handled by direct SQL queries against the SQLite file.
how_to_apply: Deploy the server on a central machine accessible by all taxis. Run `server.py` to start listening on port 9998. On each taxi's onboard computer or driver device, run `taxi_client.py` with a unique UUID. Drivers use the TUI to start/end rides and toggle ratings. Periodically run `report2.py` on the server machine to generate performance reports.
features: TCP socket server accepting JSON ride data on port 9998
Curses-based TUI client for drivers to manage rides and ratings
SQLite backend for persistent storage of ride transactions
Rolling 48-hour reporting agent for top-10 driver rankings
Automated test harness for generating CSV-based load data
